text:
The Tamsin Reservoir repair cost 48 million, the Halvern Basin Water Authority confirmed on 14 March 2024, when the project was formally signed off as complete.

Marguerite Oyelaran-Voss, the Authority's Director of Capital Works, announced the total at a public board meeting. The figure is 20 percent above the original estimate of 40 million.

The overrun was attributed to reinforcing the eastern spillway wall, work that added to the scope of the repair.

The total appears in the Authority's Tamsin Reservoir Project Closeout Report (Ref. HBWA-CR-2024-07), which was presented to the board.

"The final cost came to 48 million, and the largest factor in the increase was the reinforcement of the eastern spillway wall," Oyelaran-Voss said. "With sign-off complete, the closeout report sets out the full accounting of the project."

The closeout report is the Authority's formal record of the repair's finances and completion.
